text:
Five straight losses can make a team look over its shoulder. Columbus didn't wait long to stop looking. Zach Werenski scored 1:59 into Thursday's game at United Center, Kent Johnson made it 2-0 late in the first, and the Blue Jackets held on for a 4-2 win over Chicago that ended a 0-5-0 run.

Matthew Knies was the engine. He assisted on Werenski's opener, scored on the power play at 13:57 of the second to restore a two-goal lead after Frank Nazar's power-play goal, and set up Adam Fantilli's clincher with 31 seconds left after Spencer Knight had gone to the bench for an extra skater. Three points, first star. Werenski, at 27:12 of ice time, added a goal and an assist, and Fantilli had five shots and 1.62 expected goals of his own (expected goals measure the quality of chances, not just the count).

This was not the comfortable night the scoreboard suggests. Columbus led 25-15 in shots after two, but Chicago owned the third with 1.42 expected goals and pulled within one when Cole Smith scored at 3:52. Our deserved-to-win number, the share of replays of every shot each team wins, came out 51% Chicago and 49% Columbus. That is a coin flip, and Columbus won the toss.

The man who kept it that way was Cam Talbot. He stopped 23 of 25, saved 0.72 goals more than the shots deserved, and made the biggest save of the night on Ryan Donato late in the third. He also stopped Roman Kantserov on a 28% chance, Chicago's best look. With Jet Greaves on a six-game losing streak and Sean Monahan and Conor Garland hurt, Columbus needed exactly this kind of steady night from its veteran.

For Chicago, the bright spot was Sam Rinzel. Two assists, 24 minutes, and as Scott Powers of The Athletic noted, nine assists over his last four games. Powers also wrote that Rinzel seems to have regained a confidence with the puck that he lost last season. The Blackhawks will take that, even on a night when the two points went to Ohio.
headline: Knies and Werenski end Columbus's skid in Chicago
